title: Integral derived operations commute with finite scalar extension
statement:
Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ (inside a fixed
algebraic closure), with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, let
$f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and for
$W\in\{X,Y\}$ let
$K\mapsto K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L
=R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}_m(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m)$
be the integral scalar-extension functor [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] underlying the rational one (levelwise
modulo powers of the uniformizers), defined on derived complete objects of
$D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and carrying $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ into
$D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_L)$. For the integral derived operations
$Lf^*$, $\widehat\otimes^L$ and $R\mathcal Hom$ over $\mathcal O_E$ and over
$\mathcal O_L$ there are isomorphisms, natural in all variables,

$$
 (Lf_E^*K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong Lf_L^*(K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L),
 \qquad
 (M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong
 (M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_L}(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L),
$$
$$
 R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_E}(M,N)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong
 R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_L}(M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L,N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)
$$

for $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ (the
internal Hom being derived complete because $N$ is), and for
$E\subset L\subset L'$ they are compatible with the composition isomorphisms
$(K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_{L'}\cong K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{L'}$
and equal to the identity for $L=E$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_L$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$. The absolute-value restriction and the DVR descriptions in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give $t=uv^e$ with $u\in B^\times$ and $e\geq1$. Thus $(t^n)B=(v^{en})$. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $B/tB=B/v^eB$ is a finite set, hence a finite-dimensional vector space over $A/tA$. Choose a basis of this vector space and lift it to $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in B$. These lifts form an $A$-basis of $B$, as follows. Given $x\in B$, successively write $x_j=\sum_i a_{ij}b_i+t x_{j+1}$, starting with $x_0=x$, with $a_{ij}\in A$ chosen representatives of the residue coefficients. Then $x-\sum_i(\sum_{j<n}t^j a_{ij})b_i\in t^nB$. The inner sums converge in $A$, by completeness of $E$ in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete]; their limits belong to $A$ since its unit ball is closed. The error has norm at most $|t|^n$, hence tends to zero, proving spanning. A nonzero relation between the $b_i$ can be divided by the smallest $t$-adic valuation of its coefficients; reducing the resulting relation modulo $t$ contradicts independence of the chosen residue basis. This proves $B\cong A^d$ and also $B/t^nB\cong(A/t^nA)^d$ with one fixed basis compatible with all reductions.

proof.text: For each $W$ write $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$ as in [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Taking the inverse limit of the compatible finite-level basis isomorphisms from Step 1 gives a canonical algebra map and an isomorphism $R_W\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim} S_W$; in the chosen basis its underlying module map is $R_W^d\xrightarrow{\sim} S_W$. Indeed the subsequence $v^{en}$ has the same ordinary inverse limit as all $v^m$: extend a compatible family at indices $en$ to index $m$ by reduction from any $en\geq m$, which is independent of that choice. Finite direct sums are finite products, so taking the sheaf limit commutes with the $d$ coordinates. The map itself sends $r\otimes b$ to $rb$, so its definition is independent of the basis. In particular $S_W$ is flat over $R_W$, and tensoring with $S_W$ is an exact finite-sum functor after forgetting scalars. The coefficient reduction result [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], applied to the Noetherian DVR $A$ and its two-term free resolution $[A\xrightarrow{t^n}A]$ of $A/t^nA$, identifies $[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ with $(A/t^nA)_W$. The analogous assertion holds for $S_W$, $v^m$, and $(B/v^mB)_W$. This checks the completed, rather than constant, coefficient rings used below.

proof.text: For a complex $Q$ of $R_W$-modules define $C_R Q=R\lim_n(Q\otimes^L_{R_W}(A/t^nA)_W)$ with its specified strict-tower model. By Step 2 each quotient is the two-term Koszul complex for $t^n$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] identifies $C_R$ as the reflector onto locally derived $(t)$-complete objects. For an input $K$, [def-weil-derived-complete] provides a distinguished Roos triangle with first vertex $K$ and remaining map $1-s$ on the reduction products. The strict-tower completion $C_RK$ has another such triangle. Rotate both triangles to start with $1-s$ and extend the identity maps on the two product vertices to a morphism of triangles, using the triangulated structure [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The third map is invertible: the long exact cohomology sequences and the five lemma show it induces isomorphisms on every cohomology object. Thus $K$ is isomorphic to $C_RK$, without claiming uniqueness of this isomorphism. Since the reflector statement makes $C_RK$ locally complete, its isomorphic object $K$ is locally complete too; that same statement now shows that the canonical unit $\eta_K:K\to C_RK$ is invertible. This supplies the canonical identification used below despite the noncanonical Roos-triangle definition. Define $C_S$ similarly with $v$. We need a functorial comparison of actual strict towers, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of their Roos triangles: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] and [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] allow their product-cone models. Passing to indices $en$ preserves this model up to a natural chain homotopy equivalence. To verify it, in each block of $e$ successive coordinates write $z_j=x_j-q_jx_{j+1}$; recursively substitute $x_j=z_j+q_jx_{j+1}$ for all coordinates except the last in that block. The last equation becomes $x_{en}-(q_{en}\cdots q_{e(n+1)-1})x_{e(n+1)}$, after subtracting the finite sum of intervening $z_j$ terms. These invertible triangular changes of source and target coordinates split $1-s$ into the compressed $1-s$ and identity maps on the discarded coordinates (including the finite initial block). Identity-map cones are contractible. Every coordinate change uses a finite sum of chain maps and is natural in the tower, so it also preserves maps from a constant complex.

proof.text: Let $T_W(Q)=Q\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ denote ordinary ambient change of rings. The construction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes it on K-flat resolutions; it is just termwise tensor since $S_W$ is finite free. The integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] is $C_S T_W(Q)$: associating the tensor products identifies each reduction with $Q\otimes^L_{R_W}(B/v^mB)_W$. Restrict to $m=en$ by Step 3. Its reduction tower is then the tensor with $S_W$ of the $t$-reduction tower of $Q$. Tensor with a finite free module commutes with termwise products: in a basis both sides are $d$ copies of the same product; the canonical map, defined without a basis, is therefore invertible. It also commutes with cones. Consequently $C_ST_W(Q)\cong T_W C_R(Q)$, naturally and $S_W$-linearly, and $T_W(Q)$ is derived complete when $Q$ is. On complete inputs integral scalar extension is therefore canonically ordinary finite free change of rings. This applies to all complete objects used below, whether or not their internal Hom is constructible. The restriction to $D^b_c$ is stipulated in the statement of the item; none of the ambient comparisons uses constructibility preservation.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Let $F_R$ and $F_S$ be the ambient derived module pullbacks for $f$, with coefficient maps $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ and $f^{-1}S_Y\to S_X$. These maps are induced by the finite quotient maps and their limits; no assertion $f^{-1}R_Y=R_X$ is needed. The completed definitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] give $Lf_E^*K=C_R F_RK$ and $Lf_L^*T_YK=C_S F_ST_YK$. To check these equalities on towers, the quotient model from Step 2 identifies $F_RP\otimes_{R_X}(A/t^nA)_X$ with $f^{-1}(P\otimes_{R_Y}(A/t^nA)_Y)$; finite constant coefficient inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. K-flatness of ambient pullbacks is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The coefficient description $S_W=R_W\otimes_A B$ gives the ordinary comparison $T_XF_RP\cong F_S T_YP$: termwise both are $S_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}P$, using $f^{-1}(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y)=f^{-1}P\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}S_Y$ and cancelling $f^{-1}S_Y$ in the next tensor. In a basis this is the finite-sum comparison, and it is independent of that basis. Apply Step 4 to $F_RK$, and use that $C_RF_RK$ is complete by Step 3. This gives $T_X Lf_E^*K\cong C_S T_XF_RK\cong C_S F_ST_YK=Lf_L^*T_YK$, the first claimed isomorphism.

For $Q=M\otimes^L_{R_W}N$, the completed tensor in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] is $C_RQ$. On K-flat representatives $P,Q'$ its $n$-th term is $(P\otimes_{R_W}Q')\otimes_{R_W}(A/t^nA)_W$, since $(P\otimes A_n)\otimes_{A_n}(Q'\otimes A_n)\cong(P\otimes Q')\otimes A_n$; these identifications respect quotient transitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity topos with coefficient map $R_W\to S_W$, to obtain $T_W(M\otimes^L_{R_W}N)\cong T_WM\otimes^L_{S_W}T_WN$. Step 4 and completeness of $C_RQ$ now give $T_W(M\widehat\otimes^L_{R_W}N)=T_WC_RQ\cong C_ST_WQ\cong C_S(T_WM\otimes^L_{S_W}T_WN)$. This is precisely the second displayed isomorphism. No perfectness or termwise constructibility of the resolutions has been used.

proof.text: Write $H_R(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{R_W}(M,N)$. It is complete if $N$ is complete. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives restriction to every slice and derived currying; on a slice its two currying isomorphisms and tensor symmetry identify $R\mathcal Hom(R_U[1/t],H_R(M,N)|_U)$ with $R\mathcal Hom(M|_U,R\mathcal Hom(R_U[1/t],N|_U))=0$. Here the last vanishing follows from the local completion criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], already identified with the reduction-tower definition in Step 3. The criterion for the generator $t$ implies the criterion for all sections in $(t)$: after inverting $at$, $t$ is invertible, and the usual localization tensor/currying identity gives the same vanishing (equivalently use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-complete-elements-ideal]). Thus Step 4 identifies scalar extension of $H_R(M,N)$ with $H_R(M,N)\otimes_{R_W}S_W$.

proof.text: To prove the third comparison, use [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and a K-injective resolution $T_WN\to J$ over $S_W$, existing by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Its restriction to $R_W$ is K-injective: for an acyclic $R_W$-complex $Z$, tensoring with the finite free $S_W$ keeps it acyclic, and the termwise tensor universal property gives $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_{R_W}(Z,\operatorname{Res}J)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_{S_W}(Z\otimes_{R_W}S_W,J)$, which is acyclic by K-injectivity. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $J$ and its $R_W$-restriction remain K-injective on every slice. Repeating the acyclic-test adjunction there computes the internal Hom complexes sectionwise, and gives $\operatorname{Res}H_S(T_WM,T_WN)\cong H_R(M,\operatorname{Res}T_WN)$. In the temporary basis $b_i$, $\operatorname{Res}T_WN=N^d$. Finite sums of a K-injective resolution of $N$ are K-injective (the Hom complex out of an acyclic input is a finite sum of acyclic complexes), and the internal Hom complex commutes with this finite sum in its second argument. Therefore the canonical map $H_R(M,N)\otimes_{R_W}S_W\to H_R(M,N\otimes_{R_W}S_W)$ is an isomorphism: in the basis it is the identity on $d$ copies of $H_R(M,N)$. Its sectionwise formula is $h\otimes s\mapsto(m\mapsto h(m)\otimes s)$, so it is $S_W$-linear and independent of the basis. Combining with the preceding adjunction and Step 7 proves the third isomorphism for arbitrary complete $M,N$, in particular the stated constructible ones. This proves the derived scalar adjunction here rather than invoking the finite-Tor-only comparison of another node.

proof.text: All comparisons above come from strict-tower maps, tensor universal maps, and evaluation, so they are natural in their inputs. For $E\subset L\subset L'$, write $S'_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L',W}$. Repeat Steps 1--4 for both inclusions. The integral composition map is induced by $(P\otimes_{R_W}S_W)\otimes_{S_W}S'_W\to P\otimes_{R_W}S'_W$, $(p\otimes s)\otimes s'\mapsto p\otimes ss'$, and the completion comparisons. The two pullback routes both send a local tensor $a\otimes(p\otimes s)\otimes s'$ to $a\otimes p\otimes ss'$. The two tensor routes both send $(m\otimes s)\otimes(n\otimes t')\otimes u'$ to $(m\otimes n)\otimes st'u'$ after the appropriate ring embeddings. For internal Hom, uncurry the two routes using the termwise adjunction in Step 8: both send $(h\otimes s\otimes s',m\otimes t')$ to $h(m)\otimes ss't'$ in $N\otimes S'_W$. These equalities hold on sheaf tensors because local pure tensors generate, and commute with differentials, quotients, transition maps, products and cones. Thus they remain equal in the derived categories and after completion. The generator formulas define the maps; the bases were used only to prove they are invertible. For $L=E$, scalar extension is $C_R$ and its canonical comparison with the identity on complete objects is the completion unit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]; under this identification all three formulas are identities. This proves the identity clause in its usual categorical sense (the originally displayed functor is a product-cone construction, not literally the identity on representatives). No rational-composition statement is used to infer integral coherence.
